h1: Moving from a large brewery to a craft brewery
title: From Large Brewery to Craft Brewery | Craft Beer School
desc: What changes when a brewer leaves a large brewery for a craft brewery or brewpub in India, the skills that carry and the ones you will need to relearn.
teaser: In a large plant the system does much of the work. In a craft brewery you are the system.
standfirst: Large brewery brewers move to craft for creative freedom, smaller teams or the chance to run their own brewhouse. They bring discipline and process knowledge that many craft breweries lack. They also have to relearn hands-on work, broader responsibility and life with smaller budgets.
sections:
In a large brewery you may have specialised in the brewhouse, fermentation or packaging. In a craft brewery or brewpub, often with a brewhouse of 5 to 10 hl, you might mill, mash, boil, ferment, clean, keg, fix pumps, order malt and talk to guests, sometimes all in one day.

That breadth is exciting and exhausting. Many large brewery brewers are surprised by how much physical work it involves: lifting 25 kg malt bags, moving kegs, scrubbing manways and climbing ladders. Our guide on big brewery or craft brewery compares the two worlds from the start of a career.

Craft brewhouses often have little automation. Temperatures are set by hand, valves are manual and transfers are watched by eye. There may be no control system logging data unless you build one. Fermentation temperature may be controlled by a simple controller on each tank.

That means your process knowledge has to move from the screen to your hands. You need to know what a good mash looks like, how a transfer sounds when the pump starts drawing air and how to judge a fermentation by gravity, temperature and smell. Large brewery training helps: you understand why each parameter matters even if no system tracks it.
Your discipline is a real asset

Many craft breweries in India grew fast and still run informally. Recipes live in one brewer's notebook. Cleaning procedures vary by who is on shift. Records are patchy. A brewer from a large plant can bring written procedures, proper brew sheets, regular quality checks and basic food safety practice.

Do it gently. Nobody likes the new arrival who calls the place a mess. Start with one change that clearly helps, such as a cleaning checklist or a simple gravity log. Then build from there. Our guide on moving from a brewpub to a large brewery covers the same culture gap from the other side.
Recipe freedom comes with recipe risk

Craft brewing usually means a changing range: IPAs, wheat beers, stouts, sours and seasonal specials. Large brewery brewers often have deep lager experience but less with heavily hopped or mixed fermentation beers. Dry hopping, hop creep, oxygen pickup during dry hopping and souring all bring new risks.

Approach new styles with the same rigour you used in the plant. Test small batches first, record every change and taste critically. Ale yeasts that ferment at around 18 to 22 °C behave differently from the lager yeasts you knew. Wild or souring cultures need strict separation from your clean beers.

In a large brewery you could request spare parts, lab equipment or training through a formal process. In a craft brewery there may be no budget at all. You will improvise more, fix more yourself and argue for every purchase.

That changes how you prioritise. Spend first on what protects the beer: cleaning chemicals, sanitiser, a reliable pH meter, a dissolved oxygen check if you package. Simple, cheap quality checks often deliver more than an expensive instrument that nobody has time to use.

Large brewery brewers rarely see who drinks their beer. In a brewpub the guest may be sitting a few metres away. You may be asked to explain beers, run tastings or talk to the media. You will hear complaints directly.

Many brewers love this. It closes the loop between brewing and drinking in a way a large plant never does. If you are uncomfortable in front of people, practise. Being able to describe your beer clearly is part of the craft brewer's job.

Craft breweries are usually smaller businesses with fewer benefits and more uncertainty than large companies. Some offer more responsibility, a senior title or a stake in what you build. Weigh the whole package, not just the monthly figure. Ask about the brewery's plans and finances before you accept.

Our guide on shift brewer roles is useful for comparing what you would leave behind.

Brew one ale and one hop forward beer at home or on a pilot system before you move. Record everything. Notice where your large brewery habits helped and where you felt out of your depth. That gap is your learning plan for the first months in a craft brewery.
faqs: Is it easy to move from a large brewery to a craft brewery?
The process knowledge carries over well, but the work is more hands-on, broader and less automated, with smaller budgets and teams.
What do large brewery brewers bring to craft?
Discipline: written procedures, consistent records, quality checks and food safety practice, which many fast-growing craft breweries lack.
What will I need to learn?
Manual brewing, a wider range of styles such as IPAs and sours, dry hopping, oxygen control and working directly with customers.
Do craft breweries pay less than large breweries?
It varies widely. Weigh the whole package, including responsibility, stability and benefits. Ask about the brewery's plans before accepting.
